extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy (epistemology, philosophy of religion) and educated general readers
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length philosophical argument about the relativity of human knowledge, the necessity of postulating an Absolute (non-relative) as a datum of consciousness, and the reconciliation of Science and Religion. It discusses criteria for the validity of beliefs and the proper attitudes of science and religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: measure_of_relative_validity
rubrics_metrics.description: “The only possible measure of relative validity among our beliefs, is the degree of their persistence in opposition to the efforts made to change them; it follows that that which persists at all times, under all circumstances, and cannot cease until consciousness ceases, has the highest validity of any.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use persistence under critical scrutiny and attempts to refute as the central criterion for comparing the relative validity of beliefs. The text treats longevity/resilience of a belief in the face of opposing arguments as the primary measure of its epistemic status.

rubrics_metrics.name: scientific_explanatory_power_and_generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Science's merit lies in grouping particular relations under laws and subsuming these under more general laws, thereby arriving at causes that are more abstract yet whose actions are more completely predicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scientific theories by their ability to (a) generalize disparate phenomena under unified laws and (b) increase predictability of phenomena. The chapter treats increasing generality and predictive power as signs of scientific progress, even if the resulting causes become less intuitively conceivable.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid_unjustified_metaphysical_agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Science has often been 'unscientific' when it spoke of entities (magnetism, heat, light, electricity, etc.) as intimate and independent realities — tacitly assuming knowledge of agencies whose nature was not established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat hypothetically-invoked explanatory entities as established, independently existing realities without sufficient justification. Maintain methodological restraint: posit abstract explanatory powers or laws but avoid asserting unwarranted metaphysical attributes for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: religious_fidelity_to_recognition_of_mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion's valid element consists in its persistent recognition and diffusion of the conviction that all things are manifestations of a Power that transcends our knowledge; conversely, Religion errs when it asserts definite attributes or knowledge of that which transcends knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess religious claims by whether they preserve the core intuition of a transcendent Mystery without illegitimately claiming definite knowledge about its qualities. Authentic religious formulations should resist making precise positive assertions about the incomprehensible that undermine the very claim of transcendence.

rubrics_metrics.name: reconciliation_via_qualified_assertion_of_the_absolute
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Absolute cannot be known 'in the strict sense,' its positive existence is nevertheless a necessary datum of consciousness; supplying this qualification reconciles the philosophical, scientific, and religious perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating metaphysical or theological claims about an Absolute, require the qualification that such an Absolute is not knowable as an object of conception yet may be posited as a persistent datum of consciousness. Use this distinction (not-known-by-conception vs. necessarily posited) as a standard for reconciling conflicting accounts from science and religion.
